football_evidence.question: Can James Madison contain Troy’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.6 points.
supporting: When James Madison has the ball (third down): James Madison’s offense converts 31.8% of its third downs, and Troy’s defense allows opponents to convert 33.4% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When Troy has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Troy’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 15.4% of its runs, and James Madison’s defense stops 15.6% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Troy has the ball (big plays on the ground): Troy’s offense turns 10.0% of its runs into explosive gains, and James Madison’s defense gives up explosive gains on 4.0% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
Troy comes in on 12 days of rest; James Madison has had 7 days.
contradicting: When James Madison has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): James Madison’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.1% of its dropbacks, and Troy’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
